chunks: From him, from Safwan, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, from 'Ubayd ibn Zurarah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who has some dirhams with him; I go to him and say, 'Take them and keep them with you,' and I do not take anything back. He said, 'There is no harm in that.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no harm / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to leave money with someone for safekeeping without taking it back immediately?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this narration from Safwan ibn Yahya highlights the permissibility of *wuqf* (deposit) where physical possession is not immediately transferred, reflecting the practical financial needs of the Shia community. It establishes that the validity of the trust relies on the agreement and the trustee's retention of the funds, rather than strict immediate handover, a principle crucial for early Islamic banking and safekeeping practices.
